Kyoto rewards even a short visit, and two focused days are enough to see the highlights without feeling rushed.

## Day one: eastern Kyoto

Start early at Fushimi Inari before the crowds arrive, then spend the afternoon wandering the lanes of Higashiyama between Kiyomizu-dera and Yasaka Shrine.

## Day two: western Kyoto

The bamboo grove in Arashiyama is best seen at sunrise, and the nearby Tenryu-ji temple garden is one of the finest examples of Japanese landscape design anywhere in the country.

## Where to eat

Nishiki Market is a good stop for a quick lunch between sights, with dozens of small stalls selling everything from skewered mochi to fresh seafood.

Kyoto changes noticeably with the seasons, so if you can time a visit for the cherry blossoms in spring or the maple foliage in autumn, the same walking route will feel like an entirely different trip.
